analyst.summary: CEAT grew revenue over 22% this quarter but profit almost disappeared - down 96% - because a spike in rubber and other input costs (linked to the West Asia conflict) has outpaced the price increases the company has been able to pass on to customers so far. Management expects the cost pressure to continue into the next quarter. This is a real, industry-wide margin squeeze rather than a company-specific problem, and CEAT is using the downturn to invest in new two-wheeler tyre capacity for when the cycle turns - but until raw material costs ease or pricing catches up, near-term profitability will likely stay compressed.
